comments.author: DarkmSparks
comments.story: Cracking a 512-bit DKIM key for less than $8 in the cloud
comments.why: Explains search-space elimination like cracking Enigma.
comments.text: none of it is "brute force", GNFS is a process that rapidly excludes numbers from the search space that cannot be the answer, in principle similar to the way they broke enigma. numberphile has a great video on that one [VIDEO] Also, taking the OP as a "worse case", afaik: 512bit = $8 so 1024 = 8^2 = $64 2048 = 8^2^2 = $4,096 4096 = 8^2^2 = $16,777,216 noting $8 for 512 seems very expensive to me.

comments.author: iClaudiusX
comments.story: Forthcoming book seeks to visualise, locate and expose many numbers stations
comments.why: Succinct explanation of Enigma's exploitable flaws.
comments.text: In this case, a more relevant example from World War II might be the exploitation of flaws in the Enigma machine, namely: 1) the re-use of common phrases in weather reports, and 2) the fact that a letter could not be encoded as itself in the ciphertext, providing a mechanism of contradiction that drastically sped up elimination of possible settings [LINK] Numberphile gives a nice, succinct explanation [VIDEO]
